. mission sunday 2026: one in christ, united in mission. domhnach na misean. as we celebrate the centenary of world mission day, established by pope pius xi (1926), pope leo xiv invites us to reflect in his message for the 100th world mission day on the theme “one in christ, united in mission ”: 1. one in christ: pope leo reminds us that the church must “renew and sustain spiritual and fraternal unity ”. in a world marked by division and mistrust, our wit- ness requires “hearts that are reconciled and eager for communion ”. unity in christ is the foundation of our missionary calling. 2. united in mission: mission belongs to every baptised person: “no baptized person is exempt from or indifferent to mission ”. as pope leo emphasises, pro- claiming the gospel “is an action that is always harmonious, communal and syn- odal”. called to walk together, we must listen, share our gifts, embrace diversity and work together so that the world may believe in christ. 3. mission to love: “if unity is the condition of mission, love is its essence ”. our mission is to make god’s faithful love visible through our words, actions and ser- vice, for the church’s mission is “born of love, lived in love, and leading to love ”. we also remember with gratitude missionaries who bring christ’s love to commu- nities across the world, often amid great challenges and conflicts. today's mission sunday collection goes to missio ireland, part of the world- wide pontifical mission societies, the pope’s official charity for overseas mis- sions particularly in asia, latin america and africa. evening prayer for fr willie doyle. the parish is warmly invited to join in evening prayer (vespers) in the cathedral of christ the king, mullingar, on this sunday, 18 october 2026 at 4.00pm , marking an important moment in the cause for the canonisation of fr willie doyle sj. fr willie doyle was an irish jesuit priest who served as a chaplain to the british army during the first world war. he gave his life ministering to wounded and dying soldiers during the battle of passchendaele in 1917. his reputation for holiness has remained strong, and in 2022 bishop tom opened the diocesan tribunal for the cause of his can- onisation, with the approval of the holy see. the diocesan investigation has now reached its conclusion. following the celebration of vespers, the public conclud- ing session of the tribunal will take place in the cathedral. this is a si gnificant occasion for the diocese and for all who have a devotion to fr willie doyle. it will be the first diocesan tribunal to conclude in ireland for over forty years. fol- lowing the ceremony, the documentation gathered during the investigation will be sent to the dicastery for the causes of saints in rome. all are very welcome to join us for this special celebration of evening prayer and to pray for the con- tinued progress of fr willie doyle’s cause. cathedral closing nightly at 8 pm. vocations to priesthood: are you considering becoming a priest in the diocese of meath? vocations holy hour. st cianán’s church, duleek, co meath. friday 23rd october 7pm. live from facebook page: diocese of meath vocations. vocations contact
